newsitem.title: USA: ITT moves seen pushing Hilton to raise bid.
newsitem.headline: ITT moves seen pushing Hilton to raise bid.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp must boost its $55-per-share hostile bid for ITT Corp by more than Wall Street observers had previously expected to counter ITT's plan to break into three companies, arbitrageurs and traders said Wednesday.

Investors had widely expected a sweetening of the five-month-old bid, to at least approach ITT's recent market price in the low-60s per share. But Hilton must now weigh an even higher offer, perhaps as high as $70 to $75 per ITT share, the arbs said.

"It looks like they are effectively forcing Hilton to disappear or raise their bid. They are doing smart things. Everybody is happy, the institutions (holding ITT stock) are happy and the arbs are happy because the stock is up," said an arbitrageur who declined to be identified.
In late Wednesday morning trade, ITT shares climbed 4-1/2 to 67-1/8, easing off a new year-high 67-7/16 reached earlier in the sesion. Hilton shares added 1/4 to 29-1/4.
Earlier, ITT said it would break into three entities along business lines, spend $2.1 billion to repurchase 30 million shares, and buy back all its debt for $2.0 billion.

"I think they (ITT) did something very smart. It's a classic break-up strategy. As far as I'm concerned, the company is offering real value. They have offered a plan that investors are going to like," said Steven Cohen, director of research at Kellner, DiLeo & Co.

As the arbs recalculated their ITT valuations in light of the break-up plan, they said Hilton will at least have to sweeten its bid to $70 per share, the price of ITT's self-tender to buy back almost 26 percent of its total shares outstanding, a defensive move also announced Wednesday morning.
Hilton called ITT's plan "smoke and mirrors" and said if the company wanted to create shareholder value, ITT "should be and should have been talking to Hilton."
